newsitem.title: INDIA: India contracts for 150,000 tonnes soymeal exports.
newsitem.headline: India contracts for 150,000 tonnes soymeal exports.

text.p: Indian exporters have signed contracts for the export of nearly 150,000 tonnes of soymeal for November-December shipments, mainly to China and Indonesia, an industry official said on Friday.

"As per trade information nearly 150,000 tonnes of soybean meal exports have been contracted for November-December shipments," Davish Jain, chairman of the Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA), told Reuters.
"Contracts of nearly 55,000 tonnes with China and of nearly 35,000 tonnes with Indonesia had already been signed," he said.
Contracts have also been signed with the Philippines, Thailand, South Korea and Japan. But Jain said no details of sales to these countries were available.
Jain said Indonesia was the biggest buyer of Indian soymeal during the last two years. India exported nearly 400,000 tonnes of soymeal to Indonesia in 1995/96.
Exports to China were expected to pick up this year because of the increased demand, Jain said.
Traders in Malaysia had said the country could import up to 150,000 tonnes of soymeal for the November-December shipment.
"India was expected to export a sizeable quantity of crop to Malaysia but they have not entered the market yet," Jain said.
Overseas deals for the new crop started from $240 f.a.s (free alongside ship) and traders were currently signing deals at $265-270, Jain said.
He said India was expected to export 2.2-2.5 million tonnes of soymeal in 1996/97 (November-October).
Industry officials said India's soymeal exports in 1995/96 were expected to be around 2.6 million tonnes, higher than the earlier estimate of 2.4 million tonnes.
Jain said traders were cautious in signing fresh deals in the absence of firm crop estimates.
"The sellers are a bit cautious in signing contracts as crop size was not able to be estimated," Jain said. "But the market is slowly firming up."
Indian industry had set a soybean production target of 4.5 million tonnes for 1996/97.
But erratic weather conditions in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, which accounts for nearly 80 percent of the country's soybean production, delayed sowing.
Traders had said this could delay the harvest and the yields might be nearly 20 percent below target.
"We are mid-way between sowing and harvest but we are expecting a satisfactory soybean crop despite late sowing operations," Jain said.
